title: Chapter 102: Hensheng: To Hate Life 5
content:
Chapter 102

Taking a blade straight to the chest was brutal, but it wasn't enough to put Jiang Cheng in the ground. It did, however, leave him benched—moving hurt like hell, and tapping into his spiritual energy was completely off the table. He hated being hovered over, so when Jin Ling moved to steady him, Jiang Cheng snapped, "Get lost."

Jin Ling knew his uncle was still fuming over him running off earlier, so he swallowed his pride and kept his mouth shut. Outside, the frantic barking of the black hound echoed from down the road. A sharp, strangled yelp pierced through the rain, making Jin Ling jump out of his skin. Remembering Jin Guangyao’s kill order, he screamed toward the door, "Fairy, run! They're trying to kill you!"

Moments later, Su She burst back in through the deluge, dripping wet and visibly murderous.

Jin Guangyao raised a brow. "You didn't manage to finish it?"

"My apologies, Sect Leader," Su She spat, seething with frustration. "The damn beast has zero backbone! It puts on a brave face when it has backup, but the second things go south, it turns tail and bolts faster than anything I've ever seen!"

Jin Guangyao sighed, shaking his head. "It's likely off to fetch help. We need to wrap things up here, and fast."

"Useless trash," Su She muttered under his breath, glaring toward the back. "I'll go light a fire under them."

Jin Ling let out a quiet breath of relief. Seeing Jiang Cheng slumped on the cold tiles with a face like thunder, he hesitated, then turned toward Lan Wangji. "Hanguang-jun... are there any extra prayer mats?"

Lan Wangji had scavenged the four they were using earlier, and the temple didn't have a fifth to spare. After a quiet pause, Lan Wangji rose to his feet and nudged his own cushion toward the boy.

Jin Ling stammered, "Thank you! Wait, no, you don't have to—I can just give him min—"

"No need," Lan Wangji cut in.

He turned and sank down right beside Wei Wuxian. The two of them sat perched together on the single mat, looking as dignified as ever, and remarkably, they fit without even jostling for space. Seeing the spot cleared for them, Jin Ling scratched his head and awkwardly hauled Jiang Cheng over.

Jiang Cheng pressed hard on his own acupoints to stem the bleeding. Once settled, he flicked his eyes up, throwing a dark, fleeting glance at Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji before staring at the floorboards, lost in whatever bitter thoughts were eating at him.

Just then, an ecstatic shout erupted from behind the altar partition: "Sect Leader! We hit something! A corner's showing!"

Jin Guangyao's tense posture relaxed instantly. He hurried to the back hall, calling out, "Keep at it, double-time! Be careful with the edges—we're running out of time."

Outside, pale forks of lightning clawed through the storm, followed by rolling cracks of thunder.

Inside, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji sat side by side, Jiang Cheng sat nearby, and Jin Ling dragged his own cushion over to hover close. Under the relentless drumming of the downpour, a stifling, excruciating silence settled over the four of them. Nobody wanted to be the first to break it.

Yet for some reason, Jin Ling seemed desperate to force a conversation. His eyes darted between them before he blurted out, "Jiujiu, good thing you blocked that guqin string earlier. That would've been bad."

Jiang Cheng’s face darkened instantly. "Shut your damn mouth!"

If he hadn't let his temper flare, Jin Guangyao would have never found the opening to throw that lethal distraction in the first place, let alone pin him down. Besides, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji were hardly helpless. Even with Lan Wangji’s spiritual channels sealed and Wei Wuxian working with Mo Xuanyu’s pathetic core, their reflexes were sharp enough to dodge a wire. Jin Ling’s clumsy attempt at giving his uncle an out was so painfully transparent it only made the room ten times more awkward.

Scolded into submission, Jin Ling ducked his head. Jiang Cheng clamped his jaw shut. Wei Wuxian said nothing at all.

Under normal circumstances, Wei Wuxian would have tossed a few mocking barbs Jiang Cheng's way—teasing him for letting cheap insults get under his skin and walking straight into a trap. But after what Jin Guangyao had just laid bare, the picture was crystal clear.

Jiang Cheng knew. He knew everything.

Beside him, Lan Wangji reached out, running a firm, gentle hand down his spine. Wei Wuxian looked up. There wasn't a trace of shock in those pale eyes—only a steady, almost tender warmth.

A quiet realization struck his chest. Wei Wuxian murmured under his breath, "...You know?"

Lan Wangji gave a slow, measured nod.

Wei Wuxian exhaled a shuddering breath. "...Wen Ning."

Suibian had been in Wen Ning’s hands, yet somehow it had ended up with Jiang Cheng. And on the entire boat ride from Lotus Pier, Wen Ning hadn't breathed a single syllable about it.

"When did he spill it?" Wei Wuxian asked.

"While you were unconscious."

"That's how we got out of Lotus Pier?!" If Wen Ning had been standing in the room right now, Wei Wuxian would have glared a hole clean through him.

Lan Wangji murmured, "He felt deeply remorseful."

Frustration prickled at Wei Wuxian’s tone. "...I told him over and over, under no circumstances was he to say a word!"

Out of nowhere, Jiang Cheng’s voice cut in, razor-sharp: "Not say a word about what?"

Wei Wuxian froze, glancing up alongside Lan Wangji.

Jiang Cheng sat pressing a hand against his wound, his tone dripping with arctic venom. "Wei Wuxian, aren't you just magnificent? So utterly selfless. Pulling off such grand, heroic deeds and bearing the disgrace in noble silence—truly, it brings a tear to my eye. Tell me, should I drop to my knees and weep tears of gratitude for you?"

The raw, bitter mockery in every syllable made Lan Wangji’s face turn instantly to frost. Catching the shift, Jin Ling panicked, scrambling to throw himself between them before Hanguang-jun decided to finish what Jin Guangyao started. "Jiujiu, stop!"

Wei Wuxian’s expression tightened.

He’d never expected Jiang Cheng to welcome him back with open arms once the truth came out, but hearing the same old vitriol still stung. After a heavy beat, he muttered, "I never asked for your thanks."

Jiang Cheng let out a harsh, barking laugh. "Right! Doing noble deeds without expecting a reward—what high-minded virtue! So elevated, so above petty mortals like me. No wonder my father spent my whole childhood singing your praises, telling me you were the only one who truly embodied the Jiang Clan motto, the only one with real Yunmeng blood in your veins!"

Wei Wuxian couldn't take it anymore. "Enough."

"Enough?!" Jiang Cheng roared, his voice cracking. "You say 'enough' and that makes it law?! You're the one who has it all figured out! You're better than me at everything! Talent, cultivation, heart, soul—you understood it all, and I was just shallow and pathetic! Then what the hell does that make me?!"

He lunged forward, clawing out as if to seize Wei Wuxian by the lapels.

Lan Wangji’s arm was already moving, hauling Wei Wuxian behind his back while his other hand came down hard, swatting Jiang Cheng’s reach aside with furious precision. Even stripped of spiritual power, the raw physical force behind the strike was staggering; the jolt tore Jiang Cheng’s chest wound wide open, sending fresh crimson gushing across his robes.

Jin Ling cried out in horror, "Jiujiu! Your chest! Hanguang-jun, please, stop!"

Lan Wangji’s voice was pure ice: "Jiang Wanyin. Mind your tongue."

A few paces away, Lan Xichen quietly stripped off his outer robe, draping it over Nie Huaisang, who was curled up shivering on the floorboards. He looked up with a strained sigh. "Jiang-zongzhu, calm yourself. Shout any louder and you'll bleed to death."

Jiang Cheng shoved Jin Ling’s fretting hands away. Despite the blood loss, rage sent a feverish, violent flush straight to his head, his face twisting between chalk-pale and mottled red. "By what right?! Wei Wuxian, what gives you the fucking right?!"

From behind Lan Wangji’s shoulder, Wei Wuxian asked rigidly, "Right to do what?"

"How much did my family give you?!" Jiang Cheng spat. "I was his son! I was the heir to the Yunmeng Jiang Sect, yet for years, you eclipsed me at every turn! They raised you, and it cost us everything—it cost us their lives! My father, my mother, my sister, Jin Zixuan—all dead because of you! And what's left? An orphaned boy with no parents to raise him!"

Jin Ling flinched, his shoulders sagging as his head dropped.

Wei Wuxian’s lips parted, but not a single sound came out. Lan Wangji shifted slightly, his hand finding Wei Wuxian’s in the shadows, fingers curling tight around his.

Jiang Cheng wasn't finished. The poison kept pouring out, raw and unhinged: "Wei Wuxian, who was the one who broke his word first?! Who betrayed our clan?! You tell me! Who looked me in the eye and swore that when I became sect leader, you'd be my right hand for life?! That Gusu had their Twin Jades, so Yunmeng would have our Twin Prides?! That you'd never turn your back on me, never turn your back on the Jiang Clan?! Who said that?! I'm asking you, who the fuck made that promise?! Did you choke on your own words and swallow them down?!"

His chest heaved, his voice spiraling into frantic hysteria.

"And what did you actually do? You ran off to play hero for strangers! Wen dogs, of all people! What did they ever feed you to make you defect without batting an eye?! What was my family to you?! You get to be the righteous savior who took the fall, and whenever things went to hell, oh, your hands were tied! You were forced into a corner! You had some noble, unspeakable tragedy! Tragedy?! You kept me in the dark about everything, treating me like a complete and utter fool!

"Look at the debt you owe us! Am I not allowed to hate you?! Do I not have the right to despise you?! So why the hell does it feel like I'm the one in the wrong now?! Why do I have to look back on the last sixteen years and realize I was nothing but a fucking clown?! What am I to you?! Was I just born to stand in your blinding shadow, eating your dust?! Tell me—why am I not allowed to hate you?!"

Lan Wangji stood up with lethal, sudden grace. Terrified, Jin Ling scrambled to throw his arms wide in front of his uncle. "Hanguang-jun! My uncle is hurt—"

Jiang Cheng shoved the boy aside, knocking him flat. "Let him come! You think I'm scared of him?!"

Yet after taking that hit, Jin Ling froze on the tiles.

And across the room, Wei Wuxian, Lan Wangji, and Lan Xichen all went utterly motionless.

Jiang Cheng was weeping.

Tears spilled freely down his cheeks, yet his jaw remained clenched so hard his teeth creaked. "...By what right... What right did you have to keep me in the dark?"

He curled his trembling hands into tight fists, looking like he wanted to punch Wei Wuxian, or beat his own chest, before ultimately smashing them down against the stone floor.

He should have had the right to hate Wei Wuxian with every fiber of his being. But right now, the golden core steadily circulating spiritual energy beneath his ribs robbed him of every shred of righteousness. He couldn't even despise the man with a clean conscience.

Wei Wuxian had no answer for him.

From the very beginning, he’d kept the secret buried precisely because he never wanted to see Jiang Cheng look like this.

The promises he’d made to Jiang Fengmian and Madam Yu were carved deep into his soul: take care of Jiang Cheng, stand by him, support him. Jiang Cheng was prideful and competitive to a dangerous fault; if he ever found out, he would spend the rest of his days wallowing in humiliation, unable to look himself in the mirror. It would be a permanent, festering wound—a constant, suffocating reminder that every ounce of his prestige had been built on another man's sacrifice. His cultivation wouldn't belong to him. Winning would feel like losing. He’d be stripped of the right to stand tall.

And later, after Jin Zixuan and Jiang Yanli died because of his reckless arrogance, Wei Wuxian had even less right to speak. Bringing it up after that would have looked like ducking blame—a cheap, pathetic attempt to wave his past sacrifice in Jiang Cheng’s face, begging,Don't hate me, look, I bled for your clan too.

Jiang Cheng wept silently, tears carving track marks through the grime and dried blood on his face.

Breaking down like a child in front of an audience was something he would have considered worse than death. But from this moment forward, every single day for the rest of his life, as long as that golden core hummed inside his chest, he was going to be chained to this agony.

His voice frayed into a broken, breathless rasp: "...You promised me. You said when I became sect leader, you'd be my subordinate, backing me up for life... You swore you'd never betray the Yunmeng Jiang Clan... Those were your own damn words."

Wei Wuxian bowed his head.

After a long, hollow silence, he whispered:

"I'm sorry. I broke my word."

Jiang Cheng gave a faint, shuddering shake of his head. He buried his face deep into his bloodstained palms, staying like that for an agonizing stretch, before a dry, hollow laugh scraped past his throat.

His voice came out muffled, dripping with self-loathing: "Look at that. Even now, you're the one apologizing to me. What a precious, fragile little thing I turned out to be."
